quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly through the intersection.
You must stop and then go when the way is clear.
You must stop and then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You may turn in the direction the red arrow is pointing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop and then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop. Wait until the light turns green or a green arrow appears before you go. A posted sign may say otherwise.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely risky.
Nothing to worry about.
Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely risky.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely risky. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers in danger. Paying full attention to driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and go through carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go through carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for other traffic and pedestrians before crossing.

questions.question: How should you avoid a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive alongside them and do not tailgate.
Flash your lights at them.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive alongside them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and back. Stay away from these areas. Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.

questions.question: Taking drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the risk of a crash.
Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Reduces the effects of alcohol on driving.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can impair your driving. Mixing drugs and alcohol makes the danger much worse and increases the chance of a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: If your vehicle is about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, press yourself against the back of your seat and push your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting other vehicles. Never let go of the wheel.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming car has its high beams on and you cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the side of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. Position yourself parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, drive toward the nearest road edge.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they do not help you see much better.

questions.question: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when other drivers do something unexpected.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it will take you to stop when other drivers do something unexpected.

questions.question: You may not park closer than ____ to a railroad track.

options.text: 50 feet
40 feet
25 feet
10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 feet
questions.explanation: You may not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. Park only where you will not block traffic and where other drivers can clearly see your vehicle from all directions.

questions.question: Bicycles on the road:

options.text: Must always give the right-of-way to motor vehicles.
Do not have to follow traffic rules.
Are not a concern for drivers.
Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles on the road are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Motor vehicle drivers should respect bicyclists' rights.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:

options.text: The vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
The yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Traffic control devices in construction and work areas are:

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. Use extra caution when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers on the road.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.
No passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is ahead. The road splits into two one-way roadways separated by a median. You must keep to the right.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. You should:

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Speed up to keep your right-of-way.
Always keep your current position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When possible, make room to let vehicles merge into your lane.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.
Not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an approaching vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distances and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night drives
Uphill inclines

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distances and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle hits in a collision.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should slow to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to slow down. The new speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
They may follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or horns and red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move when the way is clear.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Merge right and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren, no matter which direction it is traveling. Drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately. If you are in an intersection, pass through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: You must use a turn signal whenever you pull away from a curb.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road ahead curves left then right.
The road ahead curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road will curve right, then curve left. Slow down and adjust your speed for safety.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
At the posted speed limit for the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, drive at or near the speed of the traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign:

options.text: Warns of existing or possible hazards.
Alerts drivers to school zones.
Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
Alerts drivers to food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns of existing or possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about existing or potential hazards. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: In winter, if a road looks dry, it is definitely dry.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Roads that look dry can actually be slippery and dangerous in winter. Watch for black ice, especially at intersections, off-ramps, bridges, and shady areas.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, it is safe to move back to the right lane:

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing a vehicle on the left, you can move back to the right lane when you see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.
